title: Three Maine Oyster Destinations Perfect for Sunny Summer Days - NewsBreak
text:
By Allyssa Marson ,
8 hours ago
As summer approaches, Maine’s oyster season feels even more special: salty air, sparkling harbors, and cold oysters served just steps from the water. If you want fresh Maine oysters and a sunny seat outdoors, these three spots are worth the trip.
In Eventide Oyster Co . in Portland, travelers line up for impeccably fresh oysters from all over the Maine coast. There is outdoor seating where you can enjoy the sunshine while watching the energy of the Old Port. Eventide has become one of the state’s most famous oyster destinations, and many visitors make a special stop in Portland just to experience its raw bar and seafood menu.
Further up the coast, Glidden Point Oyster Farms offers perhaps the most authentic oyster experience in Maine. You can sit outside overlooking the Damariscotta River, where the oysters are harvested. People travel here for the ultra-fresh oysters and the peaceful waterfront setting.
Another favorite is Oysthers Raw Bar & Bubbly in Georgetown. This seasonal raw bar has outdoor seating, a relaxed coastal atmosphere, and locally grown oysters that draw visitors from all over New England.

Whether you choose Portland, Edgecomb, or Georgetown, these oyster spots offer the perfect way to welcome summer in Maine.
Surprising Maine Foods That Smell One Way But Taste Completely Different Let’s talk about a universal truth: food can smell one way and taste completely different. Gallery Credit: Lizzy Snyder Canva Pro Baked Beans (The Underdog of Smells) Check it, if you take a whiff of your Bush's Baked Beans and you get hit with a smell like spilled molasses on a very old LL Bean boot. You’re questioning your life choices but then.. you take a bite and are transformed to a sweet, savory heaven! Canva Pro Fried Clams (Don’t Let the Scent Fool You) Everytime I smell fried clams, I get fishy, gritty, ocean funk. But not when I eat them, it's a delicious taste that could make a grown woman weep. Not to mention, the way they look.. This is the ultimate, "don't judge a book by it's cover." Amazon/Canva Pro oxie (The Soda That Smells Like Regret, But Tastes Like Victory) Moxie, I hate the taste and the smell but it is Lisbon, Maine’s very own soda and so many people love it. It smells like your grandfather's ancient medicine, but to those who enjoy it, it tastes like a refreshing flavor you didn't know you needed. Canva Pro Fiddlehead Ferns (Smell Like Earth, Taste Like Spring) Fiddlehead ferns are so very Maine. If you see someone parked on the side of the road with a basket, yanking green stemy things out of the ground, you know they are "fiddle foraging." But when you smell them cooking, it's mossy and gross. Very earthy and musty, however when you take a bite, you suddenly enjoy eating that grassy, mossy, earth. Canva Pro 5. Maine Blueberries (The Ultimate Discrepancy) Everyone knows that Maine blueberries are like royalty in the kingdom of fruit, but the kicker? Before eating one, they smell a little off. It's not that sweet smell you are expecting, it's earthy and dampy. But as we all know they taste sweet and delicious. Canva Pro Maine Breweries' IPA aka stinky HOPS We have tons of local IPAs coming out of Maine but they stink, am I right? Smelly hops can be this strong, pungent aroma, but the beer, well, it's good. Amazon Humpty Dumpty Fart Chips Humpty Dumpty Chips come straight out of Scarborough, Maine and even though they are tasty and delicious, like Lay's Potatoe Chips, when you pop them open and take a whiff, they smell like a chatty bottom.. ehem a fart. 15 Most Unusual Last Names You’ll Find in Maine Around here, your neighbor’s name might look like a typo but also be like 300 years old. Gallery Credit: Lizzy Snyder Canva Pro Labreck Say it with me now, "Labreck".. but not to be confused with "La Break," which is what we all need after shoveling our Maine driveways. Canva Pro Chouinard Don't say "bless you" after someone tells you this is their last name. It looks like a sneeze, sounds like one too. Canva Pro Rodrigue Here's a name you'll hear quite a lot! Now, remember this is not Rodriguez. Just drop the “z,” and go ahead and add a buttload of confusion. Canva Pro Dutil Guys, this last name rhymes with “futile,” especially when trying to pronounce it. Canva Pro Leclair This name is super fancy sounding, almost like like Maine’s version of royalty. Canva Pro Bouchard Okay ready? Bouchard, try saying it five times fast in a row! GO! Canva Pro Beaulieu This is such a lovely name but I wish you good luck spelling it on the first try. Canva Pro Jalbert Okay here's how we do it, this last name is half jalapeño, half Gilbert. Got it? Canva Pro Theriault Okay, I know this looks like a typo, but it isn't. Canva Pro Michaud Let me give you a hand with this one, it's pronounced: “Me-show,” not “My-chawd,” despite everything your gut and instincts are telling you. Canva Pro Veilleux This is one of my all time favorites because it was so hard for me to read. And despite what you initially feel, the “x” is just for decoration! Canva Pro Plourde This unique last name is honestly like a sound effect in a comic book. Canva Pro Gagnon This always confused me with the “gn” combo, being honestly like pure chaos in letter form. Canva Pro Daigle Daigle rhymes with bagel, just with a D. Easy. Canva Pro Quiron I love this last name, it's unusual and fittingly quirky!
